title: Tests codify duplicate tool-call IDs as acceptable
reasoning: The test suite asserts that two tool calls with the same id but different names should be preserved unchanged. Tool-call IDs are the join key used by later tool response messages, so preserving duplicate IDs makes the assistant-to-tool-result association ambiguous and can route or validate the wrong result against a call. This is especially risky because nearby tests also enforce dropping orphan tool messages by matching tool_call_id, so the contract relies on IDs being usable as unique references.
recommendation: Change the intended contract to reject duplicate tool-call IDs in a single assistant message, or normalize them into unique IDs with an explicit mapping before any tool responses are generated. Update this test to cover that behavior instead of preserving duplicates.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The current test covers the opposite behavior: it locks in duplicate-ID preservation as expected, so a uniqueness guard would fail the suite.
suggestedRegressionTest: Replace this case with a test that passes two raw tool calls sharing id=call_1 and asserts normalize/extract raises LLMAPIError, or asserts deterministic unique IDs are emitted and later tool responses can be matched unambiguously.
minimumFixScope: Update response/tool-call normalization and the provider utility test that currently expects duplicate ID preservation.
